tracks.title: Userspace launch and service image provenance
current_evidence: The build generates a userspace image archive and production artifact manifest for freestanding boot profiles.
Launch provenance, component ABI metadata, signed bundle state, and syscall-dispatched task creation are enforced in native modules.
Negative tests reject unsigned userspace launches and modeled runtime bypasses.
The production-readiness gate rejects unmarked syntheticUserspaceImage fixtures in critical launch and service test paths; existing synthetic fixtures are marked model-only.

The catalog registration path now uses an arena-backed image table with a bundle secondary index, rejects metadata-only executable registration, and rejects generated userspace artifacts when embedded ELF bytes are missing or malformed, when precomputed digests no longer match, or when generated ELF metadata and manifest state become stale.

Boot-registered userspace images now preload from the generated userspace archive on host and freestanding builds; the boot registry rejects missing or unregistered generated artifacts, and registered launch paths refuse metadata-only catalog records for all launch bundles.

Rendered-shell task launch now resolves executable metadata from the generated userspace image archive by bundle id and fails closed outside model-only tests when a configured bundle lacks a generated image.
Compositor task-view checkpoint tests now persist and restore app-linked windows for generated archive-backed app tasks instead of synthetic executable descriptors.
OS contract process-isolation checks now create contract tasks from generated userspace image fixtures instead of synthetic executable descriptors.
Host launch, service, syscall, storage, sync, and scheduler tests now use generated-image fixture readers for archive-backed executable descriptors in critical userspace paths.

The QEMU native smoke gate now requires generated userspace artifacts, scheduler binding, userspace exec/resume probes, service contract registration, service IPC connectivity, and driver restart markers before native-ready.
The service registry now rejects invalid bootstrap endpoints, zero binding identifiers, and unknown service connection flags before registering typed interfaces.

The secure pasteboard service is now generated as a userspace service image, launched through the kernel-contract service bootstrap path, published as a native service contract, and included in the service IPC connectivity proof loop.

Core manifest validation now rejects POSIX and compat.* bundle/component namespaces before application packaging, and the SDK linter delegates bundle/component compatibility checks to that manifest policy while keeping IDL text diagnostics.
production_gaps: Real-hardware proof still needs to capture the booted userspace startup and service IPC markers from the NUC11TNKi5.
graduation_criteria: Keep critical launch-path tests on fixtures derived from generated userspace image artifacts.
Keep bundle launch paths archive-backed on every build profile and reject metadata-only catalog entries for service, app, and session bundles.
Keep stale, truncated, unsigned, missing-byte, malformed-ELF, and digest-mismatched userspace archive tests in the spec and host gates.
Keep the QEMU service-startup proof exercising generated-image boot, mailbox, descriptor validation, syscall query, service IPC, fault, and restart paths before native-ready.
next_actions: Capture the service-startup marker group in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle.

tracks.title: Booted permission review and policy mediation
current_evidence: Freestanding QEMU boots now run the permission review flow before native-ready using generated app packages, the permission review service task, compositor-backed review rendering, policy mediation, and explicit grant/deny markers.

Structured permission-denial diagnostics now append fixed labels and already-materialized policy, capability, and boolean strings directly into caller-provided buffers; exact-size success and one-byte-short NoSpaceLeft failure are regression-tested, the QEMU benchmark consumes the rendered bytes through an optimization barrier, and barrier-matched current-main measurements reduce rendering by 62.9%-63.3% (500.46 to 183.56-185.53 cycles/op) with the checksum unchanged at 5,240,000.

Permission review and humane scope rendering now write fixed-schema labels, string fields, and decimal identifiers directly into caller-provided buffers; exact-output, exact-size, one-byte-short, and maximum-u64 regressions preserve visible text and bounds, the QEMU benchmark consumes the full destination buffer through an optimization barrier, and barrier-matched current-main measurements reduce render-and-grant cost by 39.5%-42.0% (5,806.41 to 3,368.08-3,511.58 cycles/op) with the checksum unchanged at 161,113,400.

Signed policy objects now live in an indexed arena with primary policy-id lookup and a scope multimap, so active-policy decisions and revocation avoid legacy first-free table scans while preserving signed generation ordering.

Capability derivation now returns a read-only borrow of the authoritative child in its fixed arena slot; the borrow may be used only while the same table instance retains that grant, and owned boundaries copy the record before revocation or removal clears the slot for reuse. Pointer identity plus copy-before-revoke and deterministic slot reuse are host-tested, while paired QEMU samples reduce workspace-object derivation by 1.1 to 1.8 percent with unchanged checksums.

The booted permission proof now feeds every Notes, Sync, and Capture review command through the xHCI HID boot-keyboard report path without the bootstrap review profile, and the native smoke contract requires explicit xHCI keyboard report, review-command, and full boot-flow command markers.

Permission review service paths reject zero audit ticks, oversized scripted commands, and rendered-surface controls before the review window exists, so profiled review flows remain bounded and auditable.

The native smoke marker contract requires review-port readiness, policy-port readiness, rendered review output, zero-authority denials, local grants, explicit device/media decisions, and lease expiry evidence.
The NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof marker file requires the same permission review and xHCI keyboard full-flow markers from real hardware serial output.
production_gaps: The booted permission proof is QEMU-backed; the first real hardware proof bundle has not captured the same markers yet.
graduation_criteria: Keep permission review markers release-gated in QEMU before native-ready and require the same markers in the hardware proof bundle.
Require real hardware input events from the NUC11TNKi5 xHCI path for at least one booted permission command before accepting the hardware proof bundle.
Reject hardware proof bundles that omit review rendering, grant, deny, and lease-expiry markers.
next_actions: Capture permission review and xHCI keyboard full-flow markers in the authenticated build/hardware-proofs/<fresh-name>/verification-serial.log single boot.

tracks.title: Live sync and private overlay transport
current_evidence: Sync state covers device graph enrollment, durable inbound/outbound frame queues, replay rejection, selective policy, per-object sharing, CRDT merge semantics, secret transfer markers, transactional database contracts, and explicit conflict review/resolution.

SyncService now rebuilds resident workspace-policy, overlay, database-contract, conflict, and transport-frame path indexes from persisted state on startup, then services selective-policy, overlay, transactional-contract id, bundle, equivalence, conflict review, and latest-frame-by-path lookups through keyed indexes instead of scanning fixed persistent arrays.

The overlay relay service rejects unauthorized relay use, target changes, empty encrypted packets, malformed zero-tick/zero-task egress requests, and relay fallback re-checks revoked device trust before enqueueing failed native sends across both disconnected/congested and post-send network-failure paths.

Overlay session opens now return an in-process, read-only borrow of the authoritative service-owned record instead of copying three maximum-sized text buffers back through the service, authority-port, and SDK layers; the lifetime contract requires a stable Service or DevNode address, and closed-state visibility plus the slot-reuse boundary are regression-tested, while paired QEMU samples reduce the full open/probe/close flow by 4.1 to 5.0 percent with unchanged checksums.

Native sync transport ABI host tests now bind captured frames to source and target task ids, require payload digests on the wire, reject zero or malformed frame headers, reject non-device or same-device endpoints, enforce packet/session metadata before encoding, reject invalid task ids before endpoint allocation, preflight packet-capture capacity and the 96-byte native endpoint/frame payload ceiling before endpoint or driver side effects, and fail closed on mutated encrypted packet metadata during decrypt.

The sync service no longer exposes its direct in-process Relay send path: end-to-end host tests replicate document, media, secret, and database payloads through NativeTransportService endpoint delivery and active-driver transmit first, use the booted relay service only as fallback, chunk payloads at the native transport ceiling, and prove object-scoped grants skip private entries while offline conflicts stay reviewable.

The two-node QEMU gate boots separate native nodes with separate native-store images and now requires booted device graph, policy, device-to-device, relay, revoked-device, persisted sync-service restart, and native driver packet-capture markers on each node.

The booted sync scenario sends encrypted native transport ABI frames through network_driver_task.sendActiveFrame, validates the captured packet equals the active driver's transmitted frame, rejects plaintext-on-wire evidence, and requires packet-captured/frame-sent, malformed-packet rejection, reconnect, replay-window rejection, and congestion-backpressure markers before native-ready.

NativeTransportService now has a production fail-closed mode that refuses endpoint delivery, packet capture, and active-driver transmit until a real Intel I225 proof with ring ownership, PHY link, tail-register writes, interrupts, MAC evidence, and the first-target network frame cycle count is attached.

TransportSession now records an explicit trust posture: relay/local-lab sessions remain local_lab_only, pinned service-identity sessions become production_attested only when verified remote attestation includes request-bound verifier metadata, and session key derivation binds the posture so lab and production sessions cannot share the same crypto context silently.

Network policy and transport session posture now require verified remote-attestation evidence with a bound verifier request digest and bound attestation verifier metadata digest before treating a pinned connection as production-attested; loose attested=true claims and root-pinned attestations without verifier metadata remain local-lab or denied for production policies.

Connection authorization now resolves each indexed network policy once and evaluates each scoped target comparison once before applying attestation pins, cutting the gated authorization benchmark roughly in half while preserving fail-closed destination and identity checks.

NativeTransportService now exposes a typed verified service-identity open path that consumes the attestation response/request, measured boot record, trusted root, and policy-pinned attestation verifier metadata digest directly; the production regression uses that path and proves a response for the wrong service identity cannot open a production session.

The native network-driver service-identity path now carries verified-attestation state, the verifier request digest, and the request-bound attestation verifier metadata digest through connection creation, key derivation, frame metadata, and brokered transmit rechecks, with regression coverage proving brokered sends keep the same verified evidence instead of downgrading to loose attested flags.

The booted sync service-path proof now provisions its network identity root through the production external-provider boundary, requires a request-bound verifier metadata digest, and persists that digest into the service-identity network policy.

NativeTransportService can now require production-attested sessions before endpoint delivery, object-share encryption, packet capture, relay fallback, or active-driver transmit; the regression gate proves local-lab relay sessions stay blocked even after I225 hardware proof while pinned attested service-identity sessions can transmit.

The rendered production journey now surfaces the object-scoped trusted-overlay share grant and drives a real offline document conflict through sync conflict review/resolution, so object sharing and conflict handling are user-visible daily-driver evidence rather than backend-only sync assertions.
production_gaps: The booted QEMU proof now observes native driver packet capture, transmit ownership, replay-window rejection, reconnect, congestion backpressure, malformed captured-packet rejection, and production-mode I225 proof enforcement, but it still uses the modeled boot network device rather than real Intel I225-LM frame receive/transmit rings.
Real-hardware evidence still needs to capture the same sync markers on the NUC11TNKi5 with the Intel I225-LM path active and packet counters tied to physical frames.

Remote device identity sessions are explicitly marked local-lab unless pinned verified attestation-response evidence with a verifier request digest and request-bound attestation verifier metadata digest is present, but production-grade remote trust still depends on the boot/attestation track wiring external providers to operational TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS roots.
graduation_criteria: Replace sync_transport_harness as the primary evidence with a native transport service that runs through endpoint syscalls and the network driver task.
Keep the two-node QEMU replication gate covering offline policy, device-to-device replication, relay fallback, revoked-device rejection, and persisted restart before release.
Bind production remote device sessions to operational attestation roots while keeping local-lab sessions explicitly labeled and rejectable by production-only callers.
next_actions: Replace the modeled boot network device in the two-node sync proof with a QEMU-visible async NIC path that owns receive/transmit rings and packet counters.
Replace external-provider software callback fixtures for production remote sessions with provisioned TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS-backed attestation roots.

tracks.title: Notes and docs daily-driver slice
current_evidence: The rendered-shell production journey is now scoped to one Notes app daily-driver path rather than a generic desktop expansion path.

The journey installs a signed native Notes package, starts its native component, opens a notes workspace and document, reviews the local object-access permission, grants an object-scoped collaborative share, syncs only after sharing, updates and rolls back the package, recovers shell/runtime state, removes the package, and revokes device and policy authority.
The share step writes a concrete trusted-overlay, object-scoped workspace grant and verifies the collaborator can read and write the shared note before sync proceeds.

The production journey surface now renders the object-scoped share proof, records the share expiry and object id, creates a conflicting paired-device replica before sync, opens a sync-conflict review surface, resolves the conflict with the local document version, and keeps that conflict-review evidence in the final journey transcript.

Task-flow ledger evidence now includes share_document alongside install_app, open_workspace, open_document, review_permission_request, sync_workspace, update_app, rollback_app_update, recover_system, and remove_app.

Ranked semantic-query results now borrow title slices from the originating indexing service's fixed document arena instead of copying a maximum-sized title into every candidate; the lifetime contract requires that service instance to remain alive at a stable address and invalidates a view when its document is updated or removed, redaction replaces the borrow with an empty slice, and paired current-main QEMU samples reduce indexing query cost by 7.5%-8.5% (585.20-586.30 to 535.35-542.00 cycles/op) with the checksum unchanged at 2,180,000.

The package-service lifecycle used by the journey now requires nonempty bounded install sources, nonzero monotonic data schema versions, monotonic active updates, stable publisher identity, stable update channels, and stable update sources before an installed Notes package can be replaced; launch plans borrow only the active revision's live component and asset prefixes instead of copying maximum-sized arrays and carrying redundant counts, reducing the gated install/update/plan/rollback benchmark by roughly 4 percent.

The Notes production journey now resolves install and update requests from a public store channel release catalog whose exact release, trusted-publisher, and bundle-to-release indexes cover exact version, latest/next, and version-regression checks. The channel refuses unsigned, signature-tampered, untrusted-publisher, or publisher-key-revoked releases; re-checks current publisher trust before resolving already-published releases; requires every published release to advance an append-only transparency sequence rooted in the previous channel root; rejects stale-root, forged-root, skipped-sequence, and per-bundle version-regression releases; carries that transparency sequence/root/log-head into package install requests, stored revisions, package launch-plan provenance, the launched task's runtime provenance record, the task debug provenance trail, and SDK debugger events/export text; records structured source fingerprints, transparency sequence, and root/log-head fingerprints on launch provenance events while keeping full roots on task launch state; rejects public-store installs without transparency evidence; rejects public-store updates that replay an already-installed sequence even after rollback; refuses launch, manifest resolution, and rollback when stored public-store transparency evidence has been stripped; exposes signed revision provenance, source identity, schema version, permission digest, signature metadata, and public-store transparency sequence to launch consumers; rejects releases without complete canonical SHA-256 supply-chain metadata; rejects releases without canonical SHA-256 asset digests and byte sizes; and rejects asset catalogs that do not match the signed manifest before producing the package install request.

The host journey now renders an ordered Notes daily-driver marker contract directly in the production journey surface for install/open, edit persistence, share/sync, update rollback, recovery/removal, authority revocation, and complete-path proof; the same marker set is required by the native-smoke cold-boot registry and the NUC11TNKi5 hardware marker contract.

The booted QEMU native smoke path now runs the ordered Notes daily-driver production journey through store:zigos/public before native-ready and emits the complete marker group on cold boot and cold reboot.

The booted shell input loop now renders typed document text, syncs the edited note, recovers runtime state while preserving the edit, and then continues through rollback, recovery, and package removal.

The bootstrapped native secure pasteboard service now replaces ambient clipboard assumptions with destination-bound, foreground-session-bound, user-gesture-bound, strictly expiring, read-once or revocable paste grants; audit events count pasteboard access and denials while redacting copied content from user-visible diagnostics.

The QEMU native smoke path now drives the booted Notes shell input loop with real text input, verifies the object-store payload equals the typed note, syncs that version device-to-device, recovers the shell/runtime checkpoint, and requires typed edit, typed sync, typed recovery, and typed-loop-complete markers before native-ready.
production_gaps: The ordered Notes daily-driver marker path and typed editor loop are now emitted by booted QEMU native smoke, but the complete path has not yet been captured on real hardware.
graduation_criteria: Keep the first daily-driver scenario narrow: Notes app install, notes workspace/document use, explicit permission review, object-scoped sharing, local-first sync, update rollback, recovery, and package removal.
Keep the ordered Notes daily-driver marker path required by QEMU native smoke before broadening desktop surface area.
Require the same journey markers in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle before calling the slice production-ready.
next_actions: Capture the complete Notes daily-driver marker group in the authenticated build/hardware-proofs/<fresh-name>/verification-serial.log single boot.

tracks.title: Userspace driver data-plane depth
current_evidence: Driver registration checks signed bundles, device-class authority, DMA range metadata, restart generations, and a PCI/NVMe-only storage target whose bus mastering is confined to brokered staging, queue, and bounce-buffer windows.

The device broker now indexes controller slots and programmed DMA domains by device using arena/index-backed tables; unconfined bus mastering is rejected, and bus mastering is accepted only as a brokered-buffer program whose declared windows enumerate the exact queue or bounce frames the real NVMe engine may touch.

The device broker is PCI-only: hosted ATA registers, backing storage, transfer cursors, write staging, and the legacy bootstrap driver modules are absent from every build. The four-slot controller arena retains its 512-byte freestanding budget while DMA programs remain generation-scoped and IOMMU-window confined.

Storage driver tasks attach through a generation-scoped PCI controller session, validate their device authority at activation time, program the NVMe DMA envelope, and attach only capacity-checked NVMe publications to the freestanding volume.

The storage controller boundary gates authorize brokered DMA buffers and reject out-of-window DMA, stale task generations, stale DMA buffers, stale broker generations, expired leases, explicit PCI controller revocation, and post-restart target-generation mismatches.
The storage data-plane gate covers active-I/O restart, DMA fault containment, partial-transfer rejection, controller revocation, and explicit republish/rebind before post-restart I/O.

The native network driver path reauthorizes brokered service-identity sends through the egress broker, so revoked network-policy capabilities stop already-open userspace network paths before transmit; network activation now fails closed until the published transport device id matches detected production Intel I225-LM inventory, and the booted sync path captures an encrypted native transport ABI frame that matches the active network driver transmit.

Driver broker, runtime lease, storage-driver attach, and driver-boundary spec tests now create runnable driver/control/app tasks from generated userspace image fixtures instead of synthetic executable descriptors, and the production-readiness gate rejects synthetic descriptors in those driver data-path sources.

A native accelerator driver task now owns brokered GPU, NPU, and media queue sessions, requires hardware queue ownership plus completion-interrupt evidence, emits typed scheduler queue events only after rejecting CPU engines, missing brokers, missing owners, missing generations, missing interrupts, and stale completions, and the booted driver proof now emits queue-owned and completion-interrupt markers required by native smoke and the NUC11TNKi5 hardware marker contract.

QEMU driver restart proof performs NVMe-backed storage reads and writes before and after restart, contains out-of-window DMA faults, rejects partial-sector transfers, stale authority, stale DMA buffers, explicit PCI controller revocation, and stale broker generations, then gates republish/rebind before post-restart I/O; the expanded marker group is required by the real-hardware proof marker contract.
production_gaps: Bootstrap storage has the deepest hardware-like data-plane proof; network now has booted encrypted frame ownership evidence and accelerator queues now have brokered driver-event evidence, but other driver classes remain inventory, policy, or publication proofs.
IOMMU and DMA isolation now have executable native programming and brokered-buffer evidence, but not real VT-d/AMD-Vi page-table programming or device fault capture.

QEMU coverage now gates brokered restart, timeout propagation, partial-sector rejection, explicit broker revocation, republish, and rebind; real hardware packet/block I/O evidence and mid-transfer device-fault capture are still pending.
graduation_criteria: Add broker-mediated data-plane tests for at least storage and network that run in QEMU and prove no kernel direct publication for excluded subsystems.
Replace the native IOMMU model with real hardware programming and fault evidence before broadening the first production target beyond brokered programmed-I/O storage.

Keep unconfined bus-master DMA fail-closed, and keep confined bus-master programs (the NVMe queue/bounce windows) modeled-evidence-only, until hardware IOMMU programming, queued invalidation, interrupt remapping, and captured device-fault records are present in the hardware proof bundle.
Gate driver restart on active I/O recovery, broker revocation, rebind, and no stale DMA or port access after generation change.
next_actions: Capture hardware packet/block I/O traces for timeout, mid-transfer fault, and post-restart recovery on the first production target.
Bind the native DMA-domain model, including the confined NVMe bus-master windows, to real VT-d/AMD-Vi programming and archive device-fault evidence before treating DMA isolation as hardware-enforced.
Capture the expanded driver restart/rebind marker group, including DMA-domain and brokered-buffer markers, in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle.

tracks.title: Resource scheduler and live platform telemetry
current_evidence: Scheduler decisions account for resource class, engine availability, thermal pressure, battery saver, privacy mode, CPU budget, memory bandwidth, and zero-copy shared memory.

Freestanding MMU mappings now use compact u16 intrusive links and a canonical per-object head/count instead of a second object multimap; mapping records retain only identity, domain, and virtual-address state, while descriptors derive immutable and generation fields from the arena-owned object on demand. Low-level mutation and descriptor methods are private so caller-owned object copies cannot corrupt list metadata, and regressions cover head/middle/tail unlinking, forced cross-object reuse of a freed slot, duplicate-versus-full errors, and revocation of a saturated mapping arena. Paired ReleaseFast builds reduce production writable load by 20,480 bytes (13,043,908 to 13,023,428) and verification writable load by 45,056 bytes (21,371,076 to 21,326,020); paired default builds reduce them by 24,576 and 45,056 bytes respectively. Two exact-head CI accelerator claim/release samples measure 78,111.62-84,944.26 cycles per operation versus 123,228.26-123,573.16 on current main, a 31.1-36.8 percent reduction with the checksum unchanged at 100,000; the checked-in baseline uses the slower exact-head sample and the hard ceiling is 260,000 cycles per operation.
Booted provider tests derive hardware-source telemetry from live runtime counters instead of purely synthetic state.
Telemetry now flows through an explicit provider boundary with test-only host fakes and production freestanding provider descriptors.
Negative tests require complete hardware telemetry before waking hardware queues.

Scheduler host tests now create runnable task records from generated userspace image fixtures, so dispatch, throttling, and fairness checks exercise archive-backed executable metadata instead of synthetic image descriptors.

The OS contract now treats background activity as a first-class native policy surface, and the dispatcher enforces signed duration, CPU, memory, remote-network, visibility, typed-service, overdue-work expiration, reservation release, and redacted-diagnostics gates before and after reserving work.

Media/print helper jobs now use an indexed arena for primary job lookup/allocation, insert each fully built job record without the reservation-time default payload write, keep completed jobs addressable without linear scans, and reject full job tables before taking scheduler accelerator claims; the QEMU benchmark consumes the full service state through an optimization barrier, and four barrier-matched current-main pairs keep the checksum unchanged at 80,000 while ranging from a 0.5% regression to a 2.3% reduction, so no stable headline speedup is claimed.

The notification center now stores notifications in an indexed arena with primary-id lookup plus a source/reason multimap for replacement suppression, maintains non-expiring attention counts directly, keeps expiring notices in a small index, and maintains a visible-notification order chain so latest-visible, dismiss, suppression, and attention-budget checks avoid unrelated table scans.

Sensitive capture sessions now keep active-session and active-kind indexes alongside active/privacy-indicator counters, so active-at-tick and privacy-indicator-at-tick checks walk only live capture sessions and remove entries on explicit stop or lease expiry.

The agent delegation service now indexes active delegations by generation and tracks active generation buckets, so kill-switch revocation visits stale generations directly and refreshes the lowest active generation without rescanning delegation slots.

A sustained-load scheduler regression gate keeps foreground work continuously ready while proving background and batch classes still dispatch within bounded deadline windows without missed lower-class deadlines.
Expired lower-class deadline ties now break by service debt, so a repeatedly serviced background queue cannot hide an equally urgent batch queue.

Hardware telemetry samples now carry explicit reader evidence, and scheduler accelerator wake/claim paths refuse `.hardware` GPU, NPU, or media availability until ACPI, thermal, battery, accelerator-reader, target-id, and reader-generation evidence is complete.

Platform policy signal tests now derive booted runtime telemetry counters from generated userspace image fixture tasks instead of synthetic executable descriptors, and production readiness rejects reintroducing synthetic descriptors in that telemetry source.
OS contract resource-governance checks now create foreground, background, batch, and emergency tasks from generated userspace app/service image fixtures instead of synthetic executable descriptors.

The background dispatcher now records bounded activity history in an indexed arena, completes records by primary id lookup, keeps running records in an active index for overdue expiry, keeps completed/delayed/denied/expired records in a reusable index for bounded history replacement, tracks the latest record id directly, and maintains active dispatch counts for throttling without rescanning the record table.

Background dispatch decision construction now receives only the appended record id from its private history helper instead of copying the fixed-size history record back out of the arena. Three checksum-matched QEMU samples measure 12,694.62-12,807.87 cycles per allowed dispatch/complete operation versus 13,740.50 on paired main, a 6.8-7.6 percent reduction, and the hard ceiling is tightened from 40,000 to 13,500 cycles per operation.
Task runtime address spaces now use an indexed arena alongside task records, so launch, lookup, snapshot restore, and rehost replacement paths no longer maintain a separate manual id-index table.

Task snapshot writes and address-space retirement capture now traverse only each arena's allocator-owned claimed prefix, including reusable holes, instead of its full 128-slot capacity; a cross-page sparse regression preserves snapshot slot order, cold capability, audit, and launch-provenance state, address-space correspondence, and retirement of exactly the three live address spaces through holes and slot reuse. Two alternating, configuration-matched QEMU pairs reduce the focused two-task low-occupancy write-only checkpoint gate by 23.4% and 29.8% (18,044.00 to 13,819.75 and 18,100.62 to 12,709.25 cycles per operation), with the checksum unchanged at 1,144,000.

QEMU benchmark checkpoint and scheduler-load tasks now pre-validate generated userspace app/service image fixtures and copy those archive-backed executable specs into benchmark task records instead of synthetic executable descriptors.

The first-target platform telemetry provider validates NUC11TNKi5 real-hardware reader snapshots before publishing hardware scheduler samples, rejects QEMU or incomplete reader evidence, and host tests prove partial hardware telemetry cannot grant accelerator work.

First-target telemetry snapshots can now be composed only from typed ACPI/FADT, thermal-zone, battery, and accelerator reader proofs with matching reader generations; tests reject QEMU ACPI proofs, stale thermal generations, online accelerator drivers without generations, and out-of-range thermal readings before scheduler hardware availability is published.

A first-target reader-provider boundary now binds provider role, target id, reader generation, and typed ACPI/thermal/battery/accelerator callbacks before telemetry counters can reach the scheduler; host tests reject test-only providers, target-mismatched proofs, and stale provider generations.

A concrete first-target driver callback provider now accepts raw ACPI/FADT, thermal-zone, battery, and accelerator samples, converts them into typed reader proofs, and fails closed when required callbacks are missing or samples are stale before booted scheduler telemetry is published.

The kernel hardware-proof state now retains parsed FADT firmware, boot memory capacity, thermal-zone samples, battery status, accelerator driver generations, and completion-interrupt observations under one reader generation; the native first-target adapter feeds those proof facts into the production driver callback provider and rejects missing FADT or memory evidence.

A first-target hardware telemetry driver recorder now validates thermal-zone, battery, GPU, NPU, and media driver readings against the ACPI/FADT telemetry base before calling the kernel proof recorders; host tests reject missing base proof, overheated sensors, missing battery devices, online accelerators without driver generations, and stale reader-generation updates.

The first-target telemetry recorder now has a boot/live source callback interface for independent thermal, battery, accelerator, and grid-carbon providers; tests prove missing battery or accelerator callbacks and malformed source readings fail closed before hardware proof facts update.

A first-target telemetry source registry now refuses to publish scheduler hardware telemetry until complete thermal, battery, accelerator, and grid-carbon callbacks are installed; host tests reject empty or incomplete registries before accepting installed source readings.

The first-target telemetry registry now exposes independent thermal, battery, accelerator, and grid-carbon provider slots while preserving complete-source publication semantics; host tests prove partial slot registration cannot update hardware proof facts or publish scheduler telemetry.

Captured NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof facts can now be installed through the production first-target telemetry provider slots; kernel and native tests reject missing thermal, battery, accelerator, memory, FADT, grid-carbon, and callback evidence before scheduler hardware telemetry is published.

First-target telemetry now rejects replayed same-generation thermal, battery, accelerator, and grid-carbon source sample sequences in the kernel recorder, and the native platform telemetry provider refuses same-generation reader snapshots unless every source sequence advances before refreshing scheduler hardware availability.

Grid-carbon telemetry now uses sequenced reader proofs with bounded intensity values, and scheduler hardware evidence is incomplete until ACPI, thermal, battery, accelerator, and grid-carbon observations are all present.

Userspace scheduler hardware-queue grants now require `.hardware` telemetry with complete reader evidence; emulator and synthetic telemetry can model policy but cannot wake GPU, NPU, or media queue claims, accelerator claims keep a per-engine deadline head for constant-time expired-deadline grants and a per-task claim index for duplicate/revocation paths, and low-level accelerator controllers expose an explicit production hardware-telemetry gate for direct callers.

Brokered accelerator queues now consume typed GPU, NPU, and media driver queue events with owner, broker, generation, completion-sequence, and completion-interrupt evidence; host tests and the QEMU benchmark reject missing interrupts, wrong owners, mismatched generations, and stale completions before releasing accelerator claims.

A native accelerator driver task now turns hardware-owned GPU, NPU, and media queue sessions into scheduler driver events only after ownership and completion-interrupt evidence is present; host tests prove missing ownership, missing interrupts, and stale completion interrupts fail closed before claim release, and native smoke plus the NUC11TNKi5 marker contract require accelerator queue-owned and completion-interrupt markers.

The QEMU benchmark quality gate now checks battery-saver batch delay, thermal background delay, memory-pressure delay, fairness ratio, starvation recovery, lower-class service-debt tie breaking, accelerator claim deadline priority, brokered accelerator queue ownership/completion before release, background throttling, and foreground latency under load.
production_gaps: The first-target telemetry contract now has a production callback provider, kernel hardware-proof adapter, driver recorder, source callback surface, complete-source registry, independent provider slots, and hardware-proof-backed slot installation for typed ACPI/FADT, battery, thermal, GPU, NPU, media, and grid-carbon readings before hardware accelerator scheduling, but real NUC11TNKi5 thermal, battery, GPU, NPU, media, and grid-carbon drivers still need to install their boot and live callbacks.

Brokered accelerator queues have a typed native driver task, driver event path, benchmark gates, and release marker requirements, but GPU, NPU, and media drivers still need to source those ownership and hardware completion-interrupt events from real device queues.
graduation_criteria: Introduce platform telemetry providers for the first supported target and mark emulator-only providers as test-only.

Keep scheduler latency, fairness across resource classes, service-debt tie breaking, accelerator claim deadline priority, brokered accelerator queue completion, background throttling, and thermal/battery policy transitions covered by benchmark quality gates.
Wire accelerator claims to real brokered device queues and completion interrupts or explicitly limit production support to CPU/media classes.
next_actions: Attach real thermal-zone polling, battery status, GPU, NPU, media, and grid-carbon drivers to the independent first-target telemetry provider slots and feed their captured NUC11TNKi5 proof facts into the first-target callback provider.
Emit brokered queue owner, generation, completion-sequence, and hardware interrupt events from real GPU, NPU, and media drivers into the scheduler driver-event path.
